items.headline: U.S. Stocks Rally Friday as Weak Jobs Report Dims Fed Rate Hike Prospects
items.summary: U.S. equities posted significant gains on Friday, October 2, 2026, with the Nasdaq Composite hitting a record high, following a September jobs report that indicated a slowdown in job creation and an uptick in unemployment. This economic data substantially reduced investor expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike, bolstering market sentiment. Technology stocks were a primary driver of the day's rally, concluding an otherwise volatile week for the broader market.

items.headline: Stablecoin Development Corp. Surges
items.summary: Stablecoin Development Corp. ($SDEV) experienced a significant surge, closing up 104.4% to $7.48 on Friday, trading above its 50-day moving average.

items.headline: Armada Acquisition Jumps on Merger Approval
items.summary: Armada Acquisition Corp. II ($XRPN) jumped 68.2% to $39.42 after shareholders approved its merger with Evernorth on September 30, with the transaction nearing completion.

items.headline: Tesla Climbs on Strong Deliveries
items.summary: Tesla ($TSLA) shares climbed 4.65% after the electric vehicle maker reported better-than-expected third-quarter deliveries of 486,532 vehicles, topping analyst estimates.

items.headline: Nike Tumbles on Weak Guidance
items.summary: Nike ($NKE) stock tumbled approximately 5.4% after reporting mixed fiscal Q1 2027 earnings that beat on EPS but missed on sales, and more importantly, cut its full-year guidance for revenue to fall in the high-single digits. Weakness in China and Europe contributed to the decline.

items.headline: Western Digital Falls on Overcapacity Fears
items.summary: Western Digital ($WDC) shares fell 10.2% after Toshiba announced an expansion of HDD production in the Philippines, raising concerns of potential overcapacity in the market.

items.headline: Seagate Tech Down Amid Production Expansion
items.summary: Seagate Technology ($STX) also saw a 10.2% drop, affected by Toshiba's plans to double HDD production, which sparked concerns about increased competition and oversupply.

items.headline: September Jobs Report Disappoints, Cooling Rate Hike Bets
items.summary: The U.S. economy added a mere 29,000 nonfarm payrolls in September, significantly below the anticipated 90,000 to 84,000. Concurrently, the unemployment rate edged up to 4.2% from 4.1%, and average hourly earnings growth moderated to 0.1% for the month. These figures, coupled with downward revisions to prior months' job growth, led to a dramatic decrease in the market-implied probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike in October, falling to roughly 22.7% from 64.2% a week earlier.

items.headline: Consumer Discretionary Leads, Technology Strong; Financials Lag
items.summary: On Friday, the Consumer Discretionary sector led all sectors with a 1.38% return, with technology also showing strong performance and remaining the top-performing sector overall. Conversely, the Healthcare sector lagged with a 0.03% loss, and Financials experienced a significant drop, falling to the last position in sector rankings amid broader concerns regarding credit conditions.

items.headline: Treasury Yields Fluctuate, Oil Prices Retreat
items.summary: Following the weak jobs report, Treasury yields initially tumbled but later retraced their losses, with the 10-year yield rising 4 basis points to approximately 5.28%. Oil prices also retreated on Friday, with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) falling around 2.1% to approximately $91 per barrel, partly due to a coordinated release of 100 million barrels of crude and diesel by G7 and European nations.

items.headline: Geopolitical Tensions Monitored Ahead of Fed Decision
items.summary: Beyond economic data, geopolitical developments, including President Donald Trump's deployment of 9,000 U.S. troops to the Middle East and warnings of potential strikes against Iran, remain a factor for investors and could influence the Federal Reserve's upcoming policy decisions.
